description:
Keep a dated record of your rental hours, so when your CPA asks whether you hit 100, 500 or 750, you have the answer.

Made for short-term rental hosts (STR), landlords with long-term tenants, and couples tracking real estate professional (REPS) hours.

FIND HOURS IN YOUR CALENDAR
• It looks back through your calendar for plumber visits, showings and inspections. You confirm what was rental work.
• Nothing counts until you say so.

ADD AN ENTRY IN SECONDS
• Type what you did, like “fixed the sink at Oak St, 2 hours yesterday”. The app fills in the property, kind of work, hours and date.
• Run a timer while you work, or add time later.
• Attach photos, receipts and notes to any entry.

SEE WHERE YOU STAND
• Material participation: your count toward the 100 and 500 hour marks.
• Real estate professional: your count toward 750 hours, and what share of your working time is rental work.
• Your pace to Dec 31 for each mark.
• Each rental keeps its own count, short-term and long-term.
• You and your spouse log your hours separately.

A LOG YOUR CPA CAN READ
• Every entry has a date, a property, a kind of work and who did it.
• Export it as a PDF for your CPA.

PRICING
Free for one rental. Pro unlocks more rentals and PDF export. One-time purchase, not a subscription.

STAYS ON YOUR PHONE AND IN YOUR ICLOUD
• Apple’s on-device model reads your calendar titles and notes on your iPhone.
• Your records are backed up through your own iCloud account.

LandlordHours keeps records. It is not tax, legal or financial advice, and it can’t tell you if you meet any tax test. Ask a licensed tax professional what your hours mean for you.
promotionalText: Aiming for 100, 500 or 750 hours? Your calendar finds the hours, you confirm them, and you see if you're on pace. Dated records your CPA can use.
